newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-British Gas prices Centrica float.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-British Gas prices Centrica float.

text.p: British Gas Plc on Friday revealed the bill for the planned spinoff of its gas suppy business into a new company called Centrica next month would be at least 841 million pounds ($1.41 billion).
British Gas, which after the demerger will rename itself BG Plc, said that it would shoulder exceptional charges and provisions of this amount to pave the way for the break-up.

The charges come in two large chunks, of which 341 million pounds is to cover the renegotiation of controversial take-or-pay gas supply contracts with energy majors British Petroleum Plc and Mobil North Sea Ltd.

Most such contracts were signed prior to the group's privatisation in 1986 and oblige it to buy fixed amounts of natural gas from North Sea producers at set rates even if it cannot find a market in which to sell the gas.
Such contracts played a central part in hampering British Gas's recent commercial performance when they became deeply unprofitable for the group.
The other 500 million pounds of provisions will cover restructuring, including the cost of redundancies, write downs of surplus property and specific demerger costs.

British Gas' demerger will separate the loss-making supply business, which will cease to be regulated in due course, from the profitable transportation operations, which will remain regulated by industry watchdog Ofgas.

In its listings document, Centrica, which will also house British Gas' Morecombe Bay gas fields off northwest England, said it made a proforma loss before tax of 452 million pounds in the nine months to September 30, 1996.
This was mainly the result of the absence of one of the year's two winter quarters when the business is most active.
Centrica, which confirmed that it does not anticipate to pay dividends in the near future, said several uncertainties would affect its immediate prospects.
The main uncertainties stem from the ongoing take-or-pay contract renegotiations and the opening up of the domestic household gas market in Britain to competition.
Meanwhile, British Gas said its share in the market for big industrial users, which was liberalised in the early 1990's, had continued to shrink amid stiff competition.

British Gas shareholders have to approve the demerger at a meeting on February 12. It is expected that trading in Centrica shares will begin on February 17 if shareholders approve the formation of Centrica.
Under the demerger plan, which was first announced nearly a year ago, shareholders will receive one Centrica share for each British Gas share.
British Gas chairman and chief executive Richard Giordano will be succeeded as Centrica chairman on July 1 by former Unilever boss Sir Michael Perry.
Giordano will also give up his executive role at BG, but he will continue there as chairman at half his current salary of 450,000 pounds, British Gas said.
Analysts said the demerger details contained few surprises.
"A lot has been foreshadowed in the original demerger announcement," said one industry watcher.
British Gas shares fell four pence to 216-1/2 in early afternoon trading.
